claims.says: If RediSearch returns exactly the matching stored documents and the index holds each labelled node's document, an index scan for an exact predicate returns a node iff it is labelled and passes it.
For a numeric range with at least one bound, numeric bounds and a numeric stored value on an indexed field, the index answer equals the Cypher filter, NaN and infinities included.
The TAG key encoding of strings (tag_encode_lower) is injective on byte strings: two different strings never get the same index key.
If the add and remove sets handed to Indexer::commit are consistent with the label changes, after commit the index table holds exactly the current document of each labelled entity.
For a strictly sorted list of at most 256 u64 key and value pairs, whichever leaf page format from_pairs picks reads back exactly the input list.
